subject: Learning Methods
title: Boundary Conditions Testing
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Boundary Conditions Testing.

hook.text: She thought she understood gravity until a child asked: why don't birds fall? Her explanation had a boundary gap.

buildup.text: Boundary conditions are the edges where a rule changes or breaks. Knowing the edges proves deep comprehension.

discovery.text: Teaching forces boundary testing naturally. Curious listeners ask 'what about?' questions that push into the edges.

twist.text: Experts define themselves by knowing when a rule does not apply. Novices know the rule. Experts know its limits.

climax.text: For any concept, ask: when does this stop being true? What are the exceptions? If you can't answer, you have a gap.

punchline.text: Know where the rule breaks. That is expert knowledge.

quiz.question: Why is knowing boundary conditions a mark of expertise?
options: Boundary conditions are tested most often on exams
Knowing when a rule doesn't apply proves deep comprehension
Edges are easier to memorize than central concepts
